Subject: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging constraints (FinPay)

Hi Alex / Emily —

Thanks again for taking time today to walk through FinPay's integration needs. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Pain points & goals we captured
- PII & PHI handling: need strong redaction and selective logging for payment tokens and customer PHI.
- Auditability: security/audit team requires immutable audit logs with 1 year retention and export capability for e-discovery.
- Data residency: primary processing in us-east-1; backups in us-west-2 only.
- Low-latency inference for fraud scoring (SLOs: p95 < 120ms for scoring path).
- Cost predictability: prefer reserved capacity for peak batch processing.

Current stack you shared
- Ingestion: Kafka topics (payments-stream) -> enrichment -> S3 raw buckets.
- Auth: Okta SSO for engineers; service accounts for pipelines.
- Observability: Datadog for metrics + traces; Splunk for longer-term logs.

Success criteria for POC
- No PII persisted in model logs by default; configurable redaction rules for fields (card_number, ssn, email).
- Audit log exports (CSV/JSON) for all inference requests including request_id, model_version, timestamp, routing decision.
- Demonstrate retention and deletion workflow (30/90/365 day policies).
- Meet latency targets on a 1k qps simulated workload (we'll agree on a benchmark script).

Next steps
1) I'll send an internal note to our infra engineering to confirm precise logging schema and retention tooling. (Connor CC'd)
2) Connor / Dylan to prepare a short technical note + example redaction config + SOC2 summary (attached).
3) Schedule security deep-dive (30–45m) with your SecOps team to walk through audit log format and encryption-at-rest / KMS options — propose Thu 3/12 11am PT or Fri 3/13 9am PT.

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf (summary of our controls), logging-requirements.xlsx (template we discussed).

If that aligns, I'll book the security call and loop in our Prod Reliability lead for the benchmarking session.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Retention: SecOps requires 365 days of immutable audit logs for all inference requests that touch payment data. Longer-term analytics data can be aggregated and kept separately.
2) Redaction: We need both client-side and server-side redaction options. For the POC, we want to show server-side redaction happening before any log write.
3) Deletion: For deletion requests tied to GDPR/CCPA, we need a documented workflow that ties a customer deletion event to purge from logs/kv stores and provide an audit record.

Also — curious about encryption: are logs encrypted with a customer-managed key (CMK) option? If so, we'd like details for procurement.

We'll take Thu 3/12 11am PT for the security deep-dive. Emily from SecOps will bring the data retention checklist.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging constraints (FinPay)

Alex — quick technical responses to the items you raised. Connor here (Sales Engineer).

- Retention: We support configurable retention windows per-log stream. For the immutable audit log requirement we can write a WORM (write-once) export to your S3 bucket with lifecycle rules you control; we can also provide a signed, time-stamped export for e-discovery.
- Redaction: We offer both pre-ingest client-side redaction helpers (SDK-level) and server-side redaction policies. Server-side redaction runs as a pre-log hook and we can provide example JSON rules. Redaction is policy-driven and can be scoped by model, route, or field name.
- Deletion/workflow: For regulatory deletes we support a delete-job that marks records as purged and emits an audit event. We can integrate with your identity system to tie deletion requests to user IDs; we will also include a proof-of-deletion audit artifact.
- Keys: Yes, we support CMK via AWS KMS for log encryption at rest. You can supply the key or use our managed key; procurement docs detail the SLA/rotation.

I've attached a short sample redaction config and the logging schema we propose (see logging-requirements.xlsx). I'll present these in Thu's call and can run through a small demo of a redaction rule in action.

Next: Marissa — want me to upload a minimal benchmark script and sample dataset to the HubSpot deal for the POC?

Thanks,
